post.title: Landlord kept your deposit? In some states, it costs triple
post.ig:
A landlord who wrongly keeps your security deposit can owe you triple in some states (Texas and Massachusetts); rules vary by state.
Deadlines after move-out: New York 14 days (itemized statement, or the landlord forfeits the right to keep any of it; deposits capped at one month's rent since 2019), California 21 days, Texas and Massachusetts 30 days.
Penalties: California up to 2x the deposit for bad faith (plus actual damages); Massachusetts 3x plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees; Texas $100 + 3x the amount wrongly withheld + attorney's fees for bad faith. Our math: $1,000 kept in bad faith in Texas = $3,100 plus fees.
Normal wear and tear can't be deducted. Under AB 2801, California landlords who deduct for repairs or cleaning must photograph the unit at move-out (from April 1, 2025) and at move-in for tenancies starting on or after July 1, 2025. Small claims limits: $12,500 for individuals in California, $20,000 in Texas justice court. Texas landlords don't have to refund until you give a forwarding address in writing.
Sources: CA Civil Code 1950.5 and AB 2801; NY Gen. Oblig. Law 7-108; Texas Property Code ch. 92 and Gov't Code 27.031; Mass. G.L. c.186 s.15B; California Courts.
News and education, not financial or legal advice. Rules vary by state.
